items.title: Measurable scalarization of the transverse helicity fibers

references.title: Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the transverse Hilbert space and helicity projectors of [[def-qftx-photon-helicity-bundle]]. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ there exists a Borel map $e_\sigma:S^2	o\mathbb C^3$ such that $|e_\sigma(\mathbf n)|=1$ and $P_\sigma(\mathbf n)e_\sigma(\mathbf n)=e_\sigma(\mathbf n)$. Put $X=M	imes\{+1,-1\}$ and equip it with the product of $d
u$ and counting measure. Then $$ (Tf)(\mathbf k,\sigma)=\overline{e_\sigma(\mathbf n(\mathbf k))}\cdot f(\mathbf k) $$ defines a unitary $T:\mathcal H_T^
u	o L^2(X,d
u\otimes\#;\mathbb C)$. It intertwines the helicity multiplier and projectors with scalar multiplication: $$ ThT^{-1}=M_{(\mathbf k,\sigma)\mapsto\sigma},\qquad TP_\sigma T^{-1}=M_{\mathbf1_{\{\sigma\}}}. $$ The sections are Borel measurable and need not be continuous or smooth.

items.title: Projected photon spin and orbital operators

references.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology
David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and a constant $\hbar>0$, interpreted as the angular-momentum scale. Let $M=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\mathbf n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$, and use the transverse one-photon Hilbert space $$ \mathcal H_T^
u=\{f\in L^2(M,d
u;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0\ 
u	ext{-almost everywhere}\},\qquad d
u(\mathbf k)= rac{d^3\mathbf k}{2|\mathbf k|}, $$ with the second-variable-linear Hermitian pairing of [[def-qftx-photon-helicity-bundle]]. Use its dense smooth transverse domain $$ \mathcal D=\{f\in C_c^\infty(M;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0	ext{ for every }\mathbf k\in M\}. $$ For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, let $P(\mathbf n)=I-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ and $h(\mathbf n)=i(\mathbf n	imes\cdot)$, where the cross product is extended complex-linearly and $\epsilon_{123}=1$. These are the transverse projection and helicity multiplier from [[def-qftx-photon-helicity-bundle]]; on $P(\mathbf n)\mathbb C^3$, $h$ is self-adjoint, $h^2=P$, and its eigenvalues are $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard basis and define the dimensionless spin-one matrices by $$ (S_i v)_a=-i\sum_{b=1}^3\epsilon_{iab}v_b,\qquad i,a\in\{1,2,3\}. $$ Let $J_i$ be the self-adjoint Stone generator of the rotation subgroup about $e_i$ supplied by [[thm-qftx-photon-rotations-helicity]], with convention $U(R_{e_i}(t))=e^{-itJ_i/\hbar}$. Define the bounded projected spin operator and its orbital remainder by $$ S_i'=M_{\hbar P(\mathbf n)S_iP(\mathbf n)}=M_{\hbar n_i h(\mathbf n)},\qquad L_i'=J_i-S_i'\quad	ext{on the exact domain }D(J_i). $$ Here $M_Af(\mathbf k)=A(\mathbf n(\mathbf k))f(\mathbf k)$ for a matrix field $A$; the proof below establishes the equality of the two formulas for $S_i'$, boundedness, self-adjointness, and invariance of $\mathcal D$. The label “projected spin” denotes this operator family and does not assert that its components form a spin-$1$ representation.

items.title: The smooth transverse domain is a core for photon rotation generators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and $\hbar>0$. Let $\mathcal H_T^
u$, $\mathcal D$, $U(R)$, and the self-adjoint rotation generators $J_{\mathbf a}$ be as defined in [[def-qftx-photon-helicity-bundle]] and [[thm-qftx-photon-rotations-helicity]]. For every unit axis $\mathbf a\in S^2$, $\mathcal D$ is a core for $J_{\mathbf a}$: it is contained in $D(J_{\mathbf a})$ and is dense in that domain for the graph norm $$ \|f\|_{J_{\mathbf a}}= igl(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_T^
u}^2+\|J_{\mathbf a}f\|_{\mathcal H_T^
u}^2 igr)^{1/2}. $$ In particular, $\mathcal D$ is a common core for the three Cartesian rotation generators.

items.title: Projected angular parts are not two independent rotation algebras

references.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and $\hbar>0$, and use the operators and domain of [[def-qftx-photon-projected-angular]] and [[thm-qftx-photon-rotations-helicity]]. The smooth transverse domain $\mathcal D$ is a common graph core for $J_i$ and $L_i'$ for $i=1,2,3$. Each $L_i'=J_i-S_i'$ is self-adjoint on the exact domain $D(J_i)$, and each $S_i'$ is bounded self-adjoint. On $\mathcal D$, with $[A,B]=AB-BA$, $$ [J_i,J_j]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^3\epsilon_{ijk}J_k,\qquad [S_i',S_j']=0,\qquad [L_i',S_j']=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^3\epsilon_{ijk}S_k',\qquad [L_i',L_j']=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^3\epsilon_{ijk}(L_k'-S_k'). $$ Thus the projected spin and orbital parts are not two commuting independent $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ representations. The commutators are asserted on the common invariant core, not as identities of unrestricted products of unbounded operators.

items.title: Second-quantized total rotations and helicity counts

references.title: Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology
Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, $\hbar>0$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T^
u)$ of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. For $R\in SO(3)$ define the Fock rotation by $$ \Gamma(U(R))= igoplus_{n\ge0}U(R)^{\otimes_s n}, $$ where the vacuum sector $n=0$ carries the identity. This is a strongly continuous unitary representation. For a unit axis $\mathbf a$, its Stone generator $J_{\mathbf a}^{\mathrm F}$ is self-adjoint on its exact Stone domain and on finite symmetric tensors with factors in $D(J_{\mathbf a})$ acts as the sector sum $$ d\Gamma(J_{\mathbf a})=\sum_{r=1}^{n} I^{\otimes(r-1)}\otimes J_{\mathbf a}\otimes I^{\otimes(n-r)}. $$ In this statement $d\Gamma(J_{\mathbf a})$ denotes that Stone generator; the formula specifies its action on the stated finite-particle domain. Let $\mathscr D_{m fin}(\mathcal D)$ be the vacuum plus the finite linear span of symmetrized elementary tensors whose one-particle factors lie in $\mathcal D$. It is a dense invariant domain, and on it the Fock total generators satisfy $[J_i^{\mathrm F},J_j^{\mathrm F}]=i\hbar\sum_k\epsilon_{ijk}J_k^{\mathrm F}$. For helicity $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, define $N_\sigma$ on the $n$-particle sector by $$ N_\sigma^{(n)}=\sum_{r=1}^n I^{\otimes(r-1)}\otimes P_\sigma\otimes I^{\otimes(n-r)} $$ and use its maximal direct-sum domain $\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_n\|N_\sigma^{(n)}\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$. Define the helicity-number difference $D_h=d\Gamma(h)$ as the self-adjoint sector multiplier with $n$-particle action $\sum_{r=1}^n h^{(r)}$ and exact domain $$ D(D_h)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\left\|\sum_{r=1}^n h^{(r)}\Psi_night\|^2<\inftyight\}; $$ the vacuum term is zero. On finite-particle vectors $D_h=N_+-N_-$. With the natural-unit free radial phase $$ (V_t f)(\mathbf k)=e^{-it|\mathbf k|}f(\mathbf k),\qquad t\in\mathbb R, $$ the Fock lift $\Gamma(V_t)$ commutes with $D_h$, so the helicity-number difference is conserved by this free isotropic propagation. If $f\in\mathcal H_T^
u$ is a normalized one-photon helicity-$\sigma$ vector, meaning $\|f\|_
u=1$ and $P_\sigma f=f$ almost everywhere, then $$ \langle f,S_z'fangle_
u=\hbar\sigma\int_M\cos	heta(\mathbf k)\,|f(\mathbf k)|^2\,d
u(\mathbf k),\qquad 	heta(\mathbf k)=\arccos\!\left( rac{k_z}{|\mathbf k|}ight)\in[0,\pi]. $$ When $|\mathbf k|$ has inverse-length units, $t$ has length units in this $c=1$ convention. These are mathematical consequences of the specified one-photon and Fock models, not claims about a measured field or apparatus.

items.title: A conical helicity packet has reduced axial spin projection

references.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology

items.statement:
Let $	heta(\mathbf k)=\arccos(k_z/|\mathbf k|)\in[0,\pi]$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$, $	heta_0\in[0,\pi]$, and $0<\delta\le\pi$, a normalized helicity-$\sigma$ packet of angular width $\delta$ is a vector $f\in\mathcal H_T^
u$ with $\|f\|_
u=1$, $P_\sigma f=f$ almost everywhere, and $f(\mathbf k)=0$ almost everywhere unless $|	heta(\mathbf k)-	heta_0|\le\delta$. Such packets exist for every $	heta_0$ and $\delta$. Each satisfies $$\left|\langle f,S_z'fangle_
u-\hbar\sigma\cos	heta_0ight|\le\hbar\delta.$$ Consequently, for any sequence $0<\delta_m\le\pi$ with $\delta_m\downarrow0$ and normalized helicity-$\sigma$ packets $f_m$ of widths $\delta_m$, $\langle f_m,S_z'f_mangle_
u	o\hbar\sigma\cos	heta_0$. An ideal delta-supported Bessel mode, defined here as a generalized amplitude supported on the exact cone $\{\mathbf k\in M:	heta(\mathbf k)=	heta_0\}$ (or a smaller fixed-radius conical shell), is not a nonzero vector of $\mathcal H_T^
u$ and cannot be normalized.
